en: Wait. Is that your grandfather's jambiyah? I thought it was a story people told over qishr.
Good news: hilt and blade are two separate pieces. Bring it to my bench and I can swap either one without touching the other.
Then swap them. Jiddi used to say a blade is only as good as the hand that mends it.
Be quick about it. A Concession patrol is working these rooftops, and their drones don't like old steel.
Courier-fixer of the souq
Engineer behind the coffee stall
Herb Seller of Souq al-Milh
Peace on you, Zayd. Four flights up to my guesthouse roof and you haven't caught your breath. Sit. Have some dry mint.
Abu Nabil. Still drying leaves above the noise of Souq al-Milh?
Someone must. When blades clash, tea won't mend you. Pink feathers close wounds; yellow clears your head for tech moves.
And the white ones bundled by the chimney?
White feathers bring a fallen friend back on their feet. For a weary crew, brew qishr: spiced coffee husks to lift everyone.
Good to know if things get rough out here.
They will. Concession enforcers stomp across these roofs, looking for contraband steel. Watch your back.
If your boots wear thin, wash your face at the sabil fountain across the roof. Clean water and quiet to catch your breath.
May your stall stay full, uncle. We will keep our eyes open.
I heard boots skidding on the tiles. You took down a Concession enforcer right under their drones.
They wanted my jambiyah. We had a disagreement about ownership.
Next time one winds up a heavy strike, have Bilqis throw her Static Net. A shock in the ribs snaps their focus and cancels the cast.
See? Even the herb seller appreciates good timing.
I appreciate quiet roofs. Cut their charges short so my pots stop rattling.
Listen down the courtyard shaft. Souq al-Milh never sleeps, even with corporate security patrols at the gates.
Spice merchants shouting over neon hum. The sound doesn't change, only the lights.
Good. When the souq goes quiet, that is when you should worry.
These clay bricks have stood five hundred years. The Concession builds with glass and plastic, but clay breathes in the night air.
Grandmother always said gypsum trim keeps out both dust and bad intentions.
It keeps out dust, at least. Against bad intentions, keep your daggers sharp.
Concession engineers tapped the main cisterns again. Cold pipe water for the rich high-rises, dry rations for the alleys.
That is why the sabil fountains matter. Free water is the only freedom left.
True words, son. Keep your head low and your canteen full.
Your jiddi stood right on this ledge thirty years back. He gave no quarter to bullies, but he never refused a stranger a cup.
He left me his jambiyah and a lot of debts.
He left you his spine, boy. The blade just reminds you to keep it straight.
They went down hard. Your drone tracker flagged their patrol route before they spotted us.
Good gear makes all the difference. Your grandfather's steel has plenty of bite left in it.
They will send more once the enforcer beacon times out. We need to stay sharp.
Then let's keep moving. If we take damage next time, remember to use the herbs Abu Nabil dried.
Right. One step at a time across these roofs.
The sabil! Cold well water, untouched by the Concession filtration tax.
Pious merchants built these fountain niches centuries ago so no traveler goes thirsty in Sana'a.
Let's wash up and rest a moment. A drink here will clear our heads and let us catch our breath.
Agreed. We drink, we catch our breath, and we press on.
Come, come! Look at this magnificent merchandise! The finest medicinal feathers in all of Sana'a!
Three hundred riyal for a single pink feather? Are you out of your mind, uncle?
Out of my mind?! Hand-plucked at dawn from the high cliffs of Kawkaban! You won't find purer healing herbs anywhere. Quality costs coin, boy!
These prices are robbery.
Your herbs look half-dead, uncle.
Surely a discount for an old friend of the family?
Keep your feathers.
Robbery?! How dare you! In my grandfather's day, we settled disputes between honorable men the old way: with steel! What do you say?
Fight Abu Nabil
Not yet
An old family friend, eh? Ha! Sweet flattery will get you far in the souq, boy... but not past my purse. Beat me in a duel, and then we will talk discounts!
You'll be back. Everyone comes back.
Oof... alright, alright! It's late anyway. Nobody buys feathers at this ungodly hour.
Fair prices it is! One-to-one, honest Sana'ani rates. But you must swear to buy herbs from nobody else on these roofs!
Here. Take this cup of spiced qishr for the road. On the house.
...That will be forty-five riyal, by the way.
Pay him
A gift is a gift, uncle.
Don't you dare, Zayd! Put that coin away. A beaten merchant doesn't charge for his apologies.
Eh, can't blame an old man for trying! Come back whenever you need fresh stock. Or if you fancy another bout!
Hmph. Sharp tongue on you, boy. A man can hardly turn a profit with relatives around.
Fine, take it and go! My stall is always open for you. And if your blade gets rusty, we can spar anytime.
Ah, Zayd! What brings you to my perch tonight?
Shop
Spar
Chat
Leave
Up you get. Again?
Sit. The qishr is still hot, and you look like a man who ran across half the souq.
Three roofs and a bridge. The guild pays by the parcel, not by the step.
Show me this parcel... That seal. It's the Concession's own.
The Concession doesn't hire couriers. It has drones for that.
Unless it wants no record. Look east, their water tower. The valve that starves this souq is at its foot.
Take these. Qishr keeps a head clear, whatever Abu Nabil burns in that stall.
Still hot. Drink, then go.
